newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cifra strong on dividend news, upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Cifra strong on dividend news, upgrade.

text.p: Shares listed by Mexican retail firm Cifra SA de CV were sharply up in heavy midday trade following an announcement that the company will propose a dividend payment, analysts said.
Cifra A, B and C class shares were all among the leading percentage gainers in Mexico. The C class had traded most heavily of the three, at 6.2 million shares, and was up 52 centavos to 12.26 pesos.
Cifra's B shares were meanwhile up 50 centavos at 12.42 pesos after 5.4 million shares had traded hands.
"It was great news. Foreigners and locals are buying; everyone is getting on board," a trader from Inverlat brokerage in Mexico City said.
"It's going great guns on the dividend news, which was a real shot from the dark. The B class could reach 13.40 pesos," a trader at Valores Finamex brokerage added.

At a shareholders' meeting to be held March 6, Cifra is to propose a cash dividend of 25 centavos per share, the cancellation of about 10.9 percent of outstanding shares and the offer of a 12.2 percent stock dividend.
Cifra also plans to release its 1996 earnings on March 6.
J.P. Morgan upgraded Cifra from to buy from market performer and Caspian Research upgraded the company to a trading buy from market performer.

"As the multiformat retailer seems to be on the verge of positive sales growth in 1997 (after roughly seven consecutive quarters of real sales declines in peso terms), we believe that the momentum for the stock is positive," JP Morgan analysts Debra Wang and Richard Long wrote.
